notes: Pixel traces of the centenary Terminalia (百年榄仁树) on lanshu-1600, read on 3-4x zooms of the photograph, and the plane assumption used to turn each trace into 3D with the calibrated camera (twin/tools/lanren_backproject.py).

A single photograph fixes only the direction of each traced point; the distance along the ray comes from the stated plane.  Plane choices are recorded per piece so that they can be revised when a second calibrated view of the tree exists.
r is the branch radius in metres, from the traced image width divided by the scale (px per metre) at the back-projected point.

trunk.basis: On the ray through the trunk centre (1205, 890) at 12.0 m from the camera.  Three independent cues agree on this distance and exclude the earlier 22-23 m reading: (1) the moss-covered root flare meets the ground at image y 930-945, which at 12 m is z 0.6-0.75 (plaza 0.60, bed 0.72) but at 22.8 m would be about z 0 - below the plaza; (2) the trunk is 104-112 px wide, 1.0 m at 12 m (1.9 m at 22.8 m); (3) the low limb tapers from 0.7 m near the trunk to 0.25 m at the boulder only with the trunk at about 12 m.  It is also 4-5 m from the centre of the sunlit crown on the Esri layer (about 43, 17.5).  Uncertainty about +/- 1.5 m along the ray (direction about 222 deg azimuth), +/- 0.2 m across it.

branches.basis: trunk centreline and width (104-120 px) on lanshu-1600, at the calibrated trunk position; crotch at z 4.2-5.0

the long low limb: leaves the crotch at z 4.0, runs east towards the camera in an S-curve (low points z 2.3 at image x 775 and z 2.15 at x 430-500) to rest on the tall boulder at z 2.3, 8.3 m from the trunk, then turns up into a stem rising from the boulder top (traced to z 4.6 at the top of the frame; above that estimated).  Plane: vertical, through the trunk and the boulder centre; stem in the plane facing the camera through the boulder.  Widths 90 px near the trunk to 50 px at the boulder; the stem is 75 px (0.36 m), thicker than the limb just before the boulder, as on the photograph.
short hanging stub under the low limb (image x 400-470, y 740-815), in the limb plane

limb rising from the low limb at its first fork (image 905, 605) and curving up to the top of the frame; assumed to grow south (towards the wing) in a vertical plane, because the photograph does not show its depth

limb leaving the low limb at its second fork (image 830, 650) and rising to the left edge of the frame, crossing behind the top of the boulder stem; assumed to run east-south-east (azimuth -25 deg), slightly behind the low limb
upright limb from the crotch (image x 1300-1380), leaning north-west in the plane facing the camera; above the frame (z 7.3) estimated
heavy limb from the crotch to the upper right corner; assumed north-west (azimuth 125 deg)
thinner limb rising up-left from the crotch (image x 1020-1150); assumed south-south-east
